A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework and experiments. Their text, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–G, and checklists are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original arrangement experiments, listener evaluations, tokenization comparisons, and instrument/chord probing results in Tables 1–5 and 8–9.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and additionally reports an analysis of listener experience and piano-reduction ratings in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: The reconstruction objective, instrument/content/history conditions, REMI-z organization, and task-specific procedures are retained. Appendix B.2 clarifies track deletion without changing its sampling rule or melody protection. The 16 attention heads discussed in v5 were already specified in v3 Section 4.1.

E1.justification: Both retain Los Angeles MIDI pre-training, Slakh2100 experiments, band/piano/drum arrangement, the same out-of-domain band scenarios, and instrument/chord probing. Additional applications discussed in Appendix F are prospective rather than newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Transformer-VAE, UNet, Composer's Assistant v2, rule-based references, tokenization variants, and ablation/probing comparators. Excluding the band baseline's style prior for objective evaluation was already specified in v3 Section 4.3.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 revises the reported baseline training status: v3 broadly states that Transformer-VAE is used without retraining, whereas v5 limits that statement to human evaluation and specifies a separately retrained Slakh2100 model for objective evaluation. Prior exclusion was already documented in v3; this limited reporting revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds an analysis of whether musical experience affects ratings of the proposed model's piano reductions, comparing listeners with more than 10 years of experience against those with at most 10 years. Existing ablations, octave-shift analysis, and probing experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v5 introduces t-tests for the listener-experience comparison. Both versions retain standard errors, repeated-measures ANOVA, Wilcoxon signed-rank testing, and the fixed training seed of 42; no increase in training runs is reported.

E6.justification: Appendix D.2 newly reports no significant experience-group differences, with p > 0.2 across the evaluated piano-rating metrics. Existing benchmark, tokenization, and probing table values remain unchanged; for example, Table 3 retains F1 scores of 85.5 for Ours and 58.3 for UNet.

T1.justification: The reconstruction equation, track-deletion sampling rule, and metric definitions in Appendix C are unchanged. Renaming V-WER to VER preserves its edit-distance formula. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified arrangement without parallel data, structured tokenization, and advantages over task-specific baselines. The conclusion's wording adjustment from demonstrating to suggesting potential does not materially redefine the claim.

C2.justification: v5 adds mechanism and metric rationales, interprets the listener-background analysis, and discusses combining rating scales with A/B evaluation and extending the framework to other applications. Appendix G removes the fixed-creativity limitation. Its added time-signature/tempo paragraph largely consolidates restrictions already discussed in v3 Appendix A.1.

D1.justification: v5 specifies REMI+ token exclusions, the 3072-dimensional inner states, the source of instrument-grouping rules, and average workloads per listener. The opening footnote replaces the future code-release promise with a demos-and-code pointer; actual external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to BART, GPT generative pre-training, and Dannenberg and Mohan's tempo study. It also adds ABC-versus-MIDI discussion and clarifies relationships to prior arrangement and denoising approaches, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites, reordered explanation around Equation 1, expanded appendix discussion, and a new Appendix D.3. Affiliations and acknowledgments are updated, including removal of template instructions. The main narrative structure remains intact, although Appendix F gains near-duplicate paragraphs.

P2.justification: All six figures and nine tables are retained. Figure 6 moves, Tables 8–9 now appear together, Table 1's V-WER header becomes VER, and front matter and page breaks change. The visual evidence is largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: Clearer baseline training documentation, tokenizer settings, and listener-workload details make the existing evidence easier to assess and reproduce. The added listener-background check supplies limited supplementary support. These gains outweigh the localized regressions from duplicated Appendix F prose and removal of the fixed-creativity caveat, but the central empirical evidence is unchanged.
